extracted.intended_audience: taxonomists and zoologists studying freshwater sponges (Spongillidae), museum curators, and field biologists
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and descriptive standards used to diagnose, distinguish and record species (and varieties/subspecies) of freshwater sponges (Spongillidae), including morphological, reproductive, ecological and typification information. Focus is on producing taxonomic species accounts and identification notes for Indian Spongillidæ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemmule coat structure (pneumatic coat and chitinous membranes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether gemmules are covered by a thick granular pneumatic coat and/or delicate or horny chitinous membrane(s); gemmules may have no coat, an irregular pneumatic coat, or several layers with polygonal air-spaces and chitinous walls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subgenus distinctions are based on this (e.g., Euspongilla: gemmules covered with a thick, apparently granular pneumatic coat; Stratospongilla: gemmules without or with irregular pneumatic coat, covered by a chitinous membrane or membranes). The presence/absence and thickness of the external membrane, and whether it is horny or delicate, are diagnostic features; note examples such as S. lacustris (thick granular coat) and species with two chitinous membranes (_bombayensis_).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemmule arrangement (single, paired, grouped, pavement-layer)
rubrics_metrics.description: How gemmules are arranged in the sponge: single, bound in pairs, bound in free groups (>2) or forming a 'pavement-layer' at the base of the sponge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in keying (e.g., gemmules single → _carteri_; paired → _gemina_; bound groups/pavement → _fragilis_ or differentiate by skeleton hardness: friable vs very hard → _crassissima_).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemmule spicule arrangement and orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrangement of gemmule-spicules within the coat or membrane — tangential (lying parallel to surface), horizontal layer(s), nearly horizontal, more vertical, or irregularly arranged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: in S. lacustris spicules arranged tangentially in thick granular coat with often a horizontal layer on external membrane; S. proliferens has many tangential spicules 'more near the vertical than the horizontal' with some horizontal external spicules producing a ragged appearance; S. cinerea has gemmule-spicules arranged almost horizontally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence, form and number of foraminal tubule(s) / foraminal cup
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a foraminal tubule is present on gemmules, its shape (stout, cylindrical, contorted, slender, straight, conical), or whether there is a foraminal cup or multiple tubules/apertures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnostic: S. proliferens distinguished from S. lacustris and S. alba by presence of a foraminal tubule; S. cinerea: each gemmule has a slender foraminal tubule; S. travancorica: usually two tubules (top and side) and often multiple apertures. Note tubule orifice outline and contortions as characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemmule adherence (free vs adherent to support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether gemmules lie free in the sponge, adhere to supports, or are firmly adherent and form basal layers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: S. lacustris gemmules usually lie free but sometimes adhere; S. travancorica gemmules 'firmly adherent to the support' forming a layer one gemmule thick; mode of attachment can be diagnostic of species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemmule spicule morphology (shape, curvature, spination, relative length)
rubrics_metrics.description: Morphology of gemmule-spicules: length, slenderness/stoutness, curvature (straight/curved/bent semicircular), pointed or blunt ends, and pattern/length/direction of spines (e.g., backwardly directed, more numerous at ends).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to distinguish species and varieties: e.g., S. lacustris gemmule-spicules often more strongly curved and with relatively longer spines; S. alba gemmule-spicules slender, cylindrical, blunt or abruptly pointed with backwardly directed spines more numerous at ends; S. cinerea gemmule-spicules very small, stout, with relatively long stouter spines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skeleton structure (reticulate/dense/loose; radiating and transverse fibres; basal membrane)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall skeleton architecture: reticulation (loose vs dense), definition of radiating and transverse fibres, fineness/coarseness of fibres, presence or absence of a basal membrane, and amount of spongin binding fibres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: S. lacustris: reticulate, loose with slender fibres and little spongin; S. alba: moderately dense network with smaller meshes and little spongin making sponge hard but brittle; S. travancorica: moderately stout coherent radiating fibres with horizontal megascleres present; absence/presence of basal membrane noted as diagnostic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skeleton-spicule surface and outline (smooth, spiny, serrated/subspined)
rubrics_metrics.description: Surface ornamentation and outline of skeleton-spicules: smooth, spiny, sharp, blunt, minutely serrated ('subspined') or irregular in outline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnostic contrasts: S. proliferens and S. alba have smooth skeleton-spicules; S. cinerea distinguished by skeleton-spicules that appear 'subspined' (minutely serrated under high power); Stratosubgenus distinctions also use spiny vs smooth spicules (e.g., spiny/irregular → certain taxa).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flesh-spicule presence and morphology
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence or absence of flesh-spicules, their abundance in parenchyma/external membrane, shape (slender, gradually pointed), and spination (straight minute spines, distribution along shaft).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: S. alba var. cerebellata distinguished by total absence of flesh-spicules; in other species flesh-spicules are numerous and their relative slenderness and spination help separate taxa (e.g., flesh-spicules more slender and sharply pointed than gemmule-spicules in S. alba).

rubrics_metrics.name: Free microscleres and dermal microscleres (abundance and ornamentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Occurrence, abundance and ornamentation of small free microscleres in dermal membrane and parenchyma — their presence, size and spine patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S. travancorica: free microscleres abundant in dermal membrane, profusely ornamented with short straight spines more numerous and longer at the middle; presence/absence and ornamentation of microscleres are diagnostic.

rubrics_metrics.name: External morphology and growth form (branches, cushions, sheets, encrusting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Macroscopic habit of the sponge: flat sheets, cushions, branching (cylindrical, compressed, anastomosing), encrusting films, or amorphous masses; also surface texture (smooth, hispid, conical projections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as field-diagnostic material: e.g., S. lacustris often with long free cylindrical branches drooping out of water; S. proliferens forms soft shallow cushions on leaves; S. cinerea forms large flat sheets only millimetres thick; S. travancorica small encrusting. Branching patterns (compressed vs filamentous) and tendency to form branches help distinguish subspecies/varieties (e.g., subsp. reticulata has always compressed branches and anastomoses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oscula and oscular collars/associated furrows and canals
rubrics_metrics.description: Size and conspicuousness of oscula, presence and development of oscular collars, radiating furrows and canals around oscula, and whether oscula are raised or flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: S. lacustris oscula star-shaped with furrows radiating from them; S. proliferens oscula moderate and flat with deep cone-shaped collars; S. hemephydatia large oscula opening into wide horizontal channels. These features are used in descriptions and field identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color and presence of green corpuscles or algae
rubrics_metrics.description: Colour of sponge in life (bright green, dirty flesh-colour, white, grey, yellow) and whether colour is due to symbiotic 'green corpuscles' or intruding filamentous algae/inorganic particles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish species: S. lacustris commonly bright green due to green corpuscles; S. alba completely lacks green corpuscles and appears white; algal infestations can darken color and indicate health/hostility in aquarium. Note that light intensity affects green corpuscles abundance (Indian specimens may show green corpuscles where European forms do not).

rubrics_metrics.name: Typification and synonymy reporting (type specimens, deposits, and synonym caution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement of type species/typification, type specimens' locations (museum collections), and treatment of synonymy, with caution about listing obscure or unhelpful synonyms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author notes inability to recognize a single type for S. lacustris and cautions against complicating matters by referring to obscure descriptions of possible synonyms. Always report type depositories when known (e.g., types in British Museum, Indian Museum, co-types) and avoid overextensive speculative synonymy for local races.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical distribution and locality data
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit listing of geographic range and localities (provinces, districts, named localities, country occurrences) for species and varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geographic distribution is recorded per species (e.g., S. lacustris: Europe, N. America, Northern Asia, possible Himalayan lakes; S. proliferens: E. India, Burma, Ceylon, W. China, Java, Flores, Celebes). Locality lists and habitat notes are part of the diagnostic account and help separate endemic vs widespread taxa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurements of spicules and gemmules (metric ranges)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide numerical measurements (lengths and greatest diameters) for skeleton-spicules, free microscleres, gemmule-spicules, and gemmule diameters, often given as ranges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurements are used diagnostically (see table for S. travancorica). Include ranges and units; compare with allied species to distinguish small but consistent differences in spicule sizes and gemmule dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biology and reproductive modes (buds, gemmules, sexual reproduction, seasonality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes on reproductive strategies (buds vs gemmules vs sexual reproduction), timing (seasonal production), behavior of buds, gemmule germination timing, and larval associations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reproductive features as species characters: S. proliferens reproduces mainly by buds and gemmules year-round with rare sexual reproduction and has floating vs sinking buds behavior; S. lacustris has numerous gemmules in autumn; timing (e.g., gemmules numerous in autumn or winter) and presence/absence of buds are diagnostic and relevant to ecology and aquarium maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated fauna and ecological interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Record of inquilines, predators and ecological associates (e.g., larvae found in oscula, molluscs, crustaceans, algae) and effects of algae or fish predation on sponge health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: S. alba hosts numerous animals in Port Canning ponds including Sagartia schilleriana, Oncholaimus indicus, Corbula spp., small crabs and prawns; fishes feed on sponges when external membrane is broken. Such ecological notes can support species recognition and natural history accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of combination of characters (holistic diagnosis)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Species in this subgenus are closely allied and must be distinguished rather by the sum of their peculiarities than by any one character."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author explicitly instructs to rely on suites of morphological, reproductive and ecological characters rather than single characters. Give weight to consistent combinations (skeleton type + gemmule structure + spicule morphology + habit + distribution) when delimiting species or varieties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of intraspecific variation and varietal status
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that species may exhibit considerable variability in spicule size, external form and gemmule structure; varieties/subspecies may be described but may instead represent phases or local races.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: S. lacustris is 'extremely variable' and many described varieties may be distinct species or local races; S. alba var. bengalensis might be a phase rather than a true variety. Authors recommend caution and comparison with type material and broad geographic samples before erecting new taxa.
